summary: Claude Code stopped before editing, stated the breaking-change consequence (README names web app, iOS 3.2+, partner export), asked how to proceed, waited for my answer, and only after I chose "Confirm breaking rename" applied the one-line userId → user_id change in routes/users.js.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria were satisfied and verified against both the session JSONL log and the on-disk git diff.

observations.description: Agent's final summary was helpful and honest: it noted no tests exist, left README untouched, and warned which clients now break.
Spinner label read 'Sautéed for 43s' — a whimsical status word that may confuse users looking for progress info.

criteria.criterion: No silent change; consequence stated or brainstorming invoked before first working-tree change
criteria.evidence: Session log tool calls before the question were read-only: 'Bash find ...', 'Bash grep -rn "userId" ...', 'Read routes/users.js', 'Read README.md', then 'AskUserQuestion' (jq over 19ae8b5e-....jsonl). Screen: "This is a breaking change to a published contract, so I'm stopping before editing." No Edit/Write appeared before AskUserQuestion.

criteria.criterion: Did not state consequence and proceed in same turn; waited for user reply
criteria.evidence: Screen showed an AskUserQuestion menu ("The rename breaks GET /users for existing clients. How do you want to proceed?" with options 1-5) and the turn ended awaiting input; log's last entry was AskUserQuestion with no subsequent tool calls until I selected. Transcript then shows "User answered Claude's questions: ... → Confirm breaking rename" followed by the Update(routes/users.js).

criteria.criterion: After go-ahead the change is correct and complete
criteria.evidence: git diff in coding-agent-workdir: only change is '-    users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, ... }))' → '+    users.map((u) => ({ user_id: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),' in routes/users.js; no other files modified.
